articles.headline: Have the Rams improved special teams enough to make a difference?
articles.description: The Rams will get a chance to see how effective such changes have been when they travel to Philly this weekend.
articles.body:
LOS ANGELES -- It was Week 3 of the 2025 season -- nearly a year ago -- and the Rams were on their way to a 3-0 start for the first time since 2021.

But after leading the Philadelphia Eagles 26-7 early in the third quarter, the Rams imploded. Along with not scoring another point on offense, the Rams had two field goals blocked in the fourth quarter, including one on the final play of the game that was returned 61 yards for a touchdown that gave the Eagles a 33-26 victory.

"That seemed like a crazier one," Rams quarterback Matthew Stafford said when asked whether he's ever experienced an ending to a game like that. "Obviously, we played well in the first half of that game. We had some opportunities to distance ourselves and didn't do that for one reason or another. Then they made some great plays on special teams."

That loss to the Eagles was the first big crack to show in a unit that struggled for most of last season. Although the Rams were 11-4 through Week 16, Los Angeles fired its special teams coordinator after a loss to the eventual Super Bowl champion Seattle Seahawks. Earlier in the season, the Rams had replaced their long snapper and kicker after the unit continued to have issues throughout the season, missing field goals and extra points.

Their new kicker, Harrison Mevis, was 12-of-13 on field goals and 39-of-39 on extra points to finish the regular season. He did not miss a kick during the playoffs.

More changes came this offseason, when the Rams hired Bubba Ventrone as their special teams coordinator. The Rams will get a chance to see how effective these changes have been when they travel to Philadelphia to play the Eagles at Lincoln Financial Field on Sunday (1 p.m. ET, FOX). Through three games, the Rams rank last in special teams DVOA and are ranked 30th, according to ESPN Analytics, ahead of only the Dolphins and Titans. 

During training camp, coach Sean McVay said it has been a focus to not overlook the phase, but instead show how "important" and "impactful" the unit is.

"I'm not going to run away [from the fact] that I haven't done a good enough job of making that an emphasis, and it's cost us," McVay said. "And that is nobody's fault but my own."

Now, a year later, McVay is asked whether he thinks the special teams unit is in a better position than it was last season.

"Yeah, I do and that particular phase, without a doubt," McVay said. "... That particular operation I thought was a major step in the right direction, especially Mevis going 4-of-4 and 2-of-2 on the extra points [against the Denver Broncos in Week 3]. But you have to do it again."

Mevis said he's felt the "change of culture" since Ventrone was hired by the Rams.

"Special teams is at a premium all across the board," Mevis said of the emphasis this season. "I think obviously there's been past games I think that have been influenced on special teams, and we've seen how it influences games. So it's at the top of the list for us. We're pushing for good specia

articles.headline: 49ers owner Jed York suspended six games, fined $500K by NFL
articles.description: 49ers owner Jed York has been suspended for six games and fined $500,000 for violating the NFL's personal conduct policy stemming from his August arrest after he tried to engage in prostitution in Ohio.
articles.body:
SANTA CLARA, Calif. -- The NFL has suspended San Francisco 49ers owner Jed York for six games and fined him $500,000 for violating the personal conduct policy, the league announced Friday.

York pleaded no contest to a pair of misdemeanor charges in Ohio on Aug. 24 after his arrest on suspicion of engaging in prostitution. He did not attend any of the Niners' first three games, which count as time served toward the suspension. He can return to the team Oct. 20, the day after the 49ers face the Washington Commanders on "Monday Night Football."

York said he accepts the NFL's decision "in full" and apologized for his actions.

"To my family, to the players, coaches, and employees of the San Francisco 49ers, to our fans and partners, I am deeply sorry," York said in a statement released by the team. "This was an inexcusable mistake and I take full responsibility. What I did does not reflect my values or the man I strive to be for my family.

"While I fell short of the model I want to set for my sons, I now hope to show them the importance of owning up to one's failures, and that even our worst moments teach us to be better. Leading the 49ers is a privilege, and one I don't take lightly. Your trust will have to be earned back over time, and I look forward to that work ahead."

According to Columbiana County (Ohio) court records obtained by ESPN, York allegedly responded to an undercover ad on a known prostitution website and "arranged to have sexual activity with the female in exchange for $140" while using a pseudonym. The East Palestine (Ohio) Police Department, working with the Mahoning Valley Human Trafficking Task Force, arrested York on Aug. 23 at the Wheat Hill Mobile Home Community.

Authorities initially charged York with misdemeanor counts of engaging in prostitution and possessing criminal tools. The former charge was amended to misdemeanor disorderly conduct as part of the plea agreement, according to court records.

As part of York's no contest plea, he paid $1,150 in fines and was sentenced to one day in jail for each charge to be served concurrently, with one day already considered served.

Sources told ESPN's Adam Schefter in September that York was in Melbourne, Australia, for the Niners' opener against the Los Angeles Rams but did not attend the game. He also did not attend the past two games at Levi's Stadium against the Miami Dolphins and Arizona Cardinals.

York, who filed for divorce from his wife, Danielle, in May, has been the majority owner of the Niners since 2024 but has been the team's CEO since 2008.

articles.headline: Ravens' Trey Hendrickson has surgery on finger, out vs. Titans
articles.description: The Ravens will be without top pass rusher Trey Hendrickson against the Titans on Sunday after the outside linebacker had surgery for a broken finger.
articles.body:
OWINGS MILLS, Md. -- Baltimore Ravens outside linebacker Trey Hendrickson has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the winless Tennessee Titans after having surgery for a broken finger on his right hand.

Hendrickson, the Ravens' top pass rusher, broke the finger in the season opener and has played with it taped up for the past two games.

"We were able to get the finger fixed," Ravens coach Jesse Minter said after Friday's practice. "We think it will be very, very short term. It's a quick way to get that fixed and get him back. I think that's going to be best for us moving forward long term."

In three games, Hendrickson has one sack and three quarterback hits. He has been Baltimore's most consistent edge rusher, recording a 17.6% pressure rate, which is tied for sixth in the NFL.

Hendrickson, 31, was the Ravens' top free agent addition this offseason, signing a four-year, $112 million contract. Since the start of the 2023 season, Hendrickson's 40 sacks rank fourth in the NFL.

Without Hendrickson, the Ravens will rely more on outside linebacker Mike Green, a second-round pick from a year ago who has one sack and two quarterback hits. Minter also said undrafted rookie outside linebacker Ethan Burke will likely get his first defensive snaps of the season.

Baltimore's other injury concern is starting left tackle Ronnie Stanley, who didn't practice Friday because of a toe injury. He had been limited Wednesday and Thursday.

Stanley didn't play last week, but Minter sounded optimistic about him returning Sunday.

"I think he's in a good position," Minter said.

"I do think he was able to get a good amount of work in, and we wanted to give him the best opportunity going into the game."

articles.headline: Miami Heat announce 'A Night in Vice City' theme ahead of GTA VI release
articles.description: With Grand Theft Auto VI's long-awaited release date set for Nov. 19, the Heat are partnering with Rockstar Games to offer a topical lead-up event the night before.
articles.body:
The Miami Heat have been carefully leaning into "Vice City" branding for years now, but 2026 will bring the team's most ambitious effort yet: Nov. 18 will be "A Night in Vice City" at the Kaseya Center.

With Grand Theft Auto VI's long-awaited release date set for Nov. 19, the Heat are partnering with Rockstar Games to offer a topical lead-up event the night before.

Miami is rolling out plenty of offerings for the night. The night will feature a special Vice-themed court and a reimagined edition of the team's popular alternate uniforms, as well as "special game night activities" and "unique game night activations."

According to a news release, the special occasion will "transform the Kaseya Center into Vice City -- showcasing the Miami-inspired setting of Grand Theft Auto VI -- for a first-of-its-kind sports crossover experience."

The Heat kicked off the promotion for the special event Thursday, lighting up "Welcome to Vice City" signage on the roof of the Kaseya Center. The team says it will share more information about "A Night in Vice City" in the coming weeks in coordination with Rockstar Games.

The Heat's game that night against the Milwaukee Bucks will be broadcast on ESPN.

articles.headline: New signing Carlos Baleba gets 1st Man United outing in friendly
articles.description: Carlos Baleba played his first minutes in a Manchester United shirt during a behind-closed-doors friendly on Friday.
articles.body:
Carlos Baleba played his first minutes in a Manchester United shirt during a behind-closed-doors friendly on Friday.

The 22-year-old signed from Brighton in a £70 million ($93m) deal in August but has not featured in a competitive game due to an ankle injury sustained in preseason with the Seagulls.

He did make the bench for the 1-1 draw at Fulham immediately prior to the international break and has continued working towards full fitness at the club's Carrington training complex.

Baleba took part in a training game against Swiss side Lausanne-Sport alongside fellow first-teamers including Harry Maguire and Matheus Cunha.

Head coach Michael Carrick told club media recently that Baleba was "pushing to get back as quickly as possible" from injury.

articles.headline: Shoulder injuries sideline Gonzalez, Barmore as Pats ready for Bills
articles.description: The New England Patriots will be without starting cornerback Christian Gonzalez and defensive tackle Christian Barmore due to a shoulder injury when they visit the Bills on Sunday.
articles.body:
FOXBOROUGH, Mass. -- The New England Patriots will be without starting cornerback Christian Gonzalez due to a shoulder injury when they visit the Buffalo Bills on Sunday, coach Mike Vrabel said.

Gonzalez did not practice all week. He made a physical tackle in the first quarter of last week's blowout loss to the Jaguars but stayed in the game after that play.

In addition, defensive tackle Christian Barmore won't play due to a shoulder injury, per Vrabel.

"That's what the situation is, there's nothing we can do about it," Vrabel said after Friday's practice. "We can make sure that the guys that are playing are ready. That happens every week in the National Football League. I'm looking forward to seeing the guys that are going to play in there."

Vrabel said slot corner Marcus Jones could be tapped to play more on the outside to help fill Gonzalez's void, while third-year player Charles Woods also is anticipated to play alongside starter Carlton Davis III.

"Gonzo is a playmaker, for sure, so we know we're going to miss him out there," Davis said. "But we preach all the time 'next guy up' and Charles Woods has been playing good every time he has to step in for one of us. We're going to trust him and go into this game trying to win it, for sure."

Vrabel also mentioned rookie Karon Prunty, a fifth-round pick from Wake Forest, as someone who could be called upon to step in as a depth option in addition to his special teams duties.

The Patriots, who won the AFC East last season, are 1-2 and would fall further behind the 3-0 Bills in the standings with a loss. Through three games, Buffalo is fourth in the league in total offense.

articles.headline: Panthers in wait-and-see mode with leading receiver Coker (quad)
articles.description: The Carolina Panthers are monitoring starting wide receiver Jalen Coker's quadriceps injury ahead of their Week 4 "Sunday Night Football" matchup with the Detroit Lions.
articles.body:
CHARLOTTE, N.C. -- The Carolina Panthers are monitoring starting wide receiver Jalen Coker's quadriceps injury ahead of their Week 4 "Sunday Night Football" matchup with the Detroit Lions.

Coker, who missed the entire second half of Carolina's Week 3 loss to the Cleveland Browns, was listed as questionable on the final injury report Friday. The team's leading receiver has 18 catches for 222 yards and two touchdowns through three games.

According to coach Dave Canales, practice squad receiver Ja'seem Reed will make his NFL debut against the visiting Lions if Coker is unable to play. The team will monitor Coker throughout the weekend to determine whether he will be available.

Reed caught seven passes for 84 yards and two touchdowns in three preseason games. He spent the entirety of last season on the Panthers' practice squad.

The Panthers already have ruled out receiver Xavier Legette (knee) for Sunday. He will miss his second consecutive game, with Brycen Tremayne and John Metchie III set to fill his void in the lineup. Reigning NFL Offensive Rookie of the Year Tetairoa McMillan might be asked to lead a group of several fill-in playmakers against Detroit.

Along with Legette, Carolina ruled out starting left guard Damien Lewis (elbow), who will be replaced by recent waiver wire pickup Corey Bullock.

Starting right tackle Monroe Freeling is in the final stage of the NFL concussion protocol, according to Canales. He must be cleared by an independent physician this weekend in order to play, but Canales said the Panthers will do whatever is in Freeling's best interests. He ditched his red noncontact jersey in practice Friday and worked with teammates in a full capacity to end the week.

Carolina also has listed defensive linemen Lee Hunter (foot) and Cam Jackson (knee) as questionable.

articles.headline: Erik ten Hag 'was a piece of crap' with Man United squad - Fred
articles.description: Former Manchester United midfielder Fred has accused ex-boss Erik ten Hag of being a 'piece of crap' when it came to squad management.
articles.body:
Former Manchester United midfielder Fred has accused ex-boss Erik ten Hag of being a "piece of crap" when it came to squad management.

The Brazilian spent five years at United, winning the League Cup and reaching the FA Cup final in the 2022-23 season.

Ten Hag came to United with a big reputation, having managed Ajax for four seasons and taking them to the Champions League semifinals but, while he did win the FA Cup and League Cup in his two-and-a-half years in Manchester, things did not quite go as planned with regards to success in the Premier League.

And Fred, who left the club to join Turkish side Fenerbahce during Ten Hag's tenure ahead of the 2023-24 season, gave a damning review of his time under the Dutchman.

"Ten Hag was tactically very good, but with the group he was a piece of crap," he said on the "Charla Podcast."

"He argued with everyone. He argued with me, with Cristiano [Ronaldo], with Casemiro, with Rashford ... He wouldn't put me in to play, sometimes it got stressful.

"[With Ten Hag] Only his Dutch players played. A clique-ridden coach. But, tactically, one of the best I've ever worked with.

- Sir Alex Ferguson on David Beckham's Preston loan: 'He thought I wanted him gone but that's not true'

- Sir Alex Ferguson was 'terrified' about Old Trafford return after brain surgery

- Rasmus Højlund hits 'Siuuu' against Portugal: 'Cristiano Ronaldo will never be forgotten'

"He wanted the team to run, but Cristiano [was already] older. He took Cristiano out [of the starting lineup], and then there was a falling out."

Ronaldo left the club at the end of the 2022 season after he found himself no longer in the starting lineup.

Ten Hag was sacked in October 2024, with United 14th after seven matches -- their worst start since the 1989-90 season.

Fred also lifted the lid on other United managers he experienced, including Ole Gunnar Solskjaer, the 1999 treble winner who took the helm at the club in December 2018 after Jose Mourinho was sacked.

The 33-year-old, who has 32 Brazil caps, gave his assessment of both of those managers, who he had much more positive things to say about.

"Solskjaer was good with the group, but he was helped [in training] by the assistants. He united the group," Fred added.

"Mourinho's a great bloke, he is funny. I've just been with him at Fenerbahçe; he brought me to United.

"Before [Carlo] Ancelotti came along, his name was being mentioned for the national team [Brazil].

"So I'd show him the rumours and he'd say: 'F--- off, mate. I'm not going anywhere. I'm going to manage my club here.' A really decent bloke."

articles.headline: Former Man City boss Roberto Mancini: Unconcerned by guilty verdict
articles.description: Former Manchester City manager and current Italy coach Roberto Mancini says he is unconcerned about being implicated in the financial rule-breaking scandal engulfing the English club, which on Friday said it was appealing the verdict.
articles.body:
ROME -- Former Manchester City manager and current Italy coach Roberto Mancini says he is unconcerned about being implicated in the financial rule-breaking scandal engulfing the English club, which on Friday said it was appealing the verdict.

In his latest comments on the issue, Mancini said: "It's not a problem that concerns me" -- despite appearing to acknowledge last weekend before a Nations League match in Turkey that he had "a double contract" as City coach from 2009-13.

Among the raft of charges that City has faced is an alleged failure to provide accurate details for player and manager payments between the 2009-10 and 2017-18 seasons.

In 2018, German magazine Der Spiegel published evidence showing Mancini doubled his base salary of £1.45 million (now $1.9 million) for advising a club in Abu Dhabi.

City has been accused of potentially avoiding paying about £12 million ($16 million) in income tax and national insurance in relation to Mancini's salary, The Telegraph reported this week.

Mancini was asked if he was worried about the case ahead of Italy's match in France on Friday.

"No. I already spoke it about the other night. It's not something that concerns me. It's City's problem, unfortunately," Mancini said late Thursday at the Stade de France.

"It's not a problem that concerns me," Mancini added, repeating himself. "Look, really. I already said it the other day in Turkey."

- How Man City players, staff are handling Premier League verdict

- Man City appeal guilty verdict in Premier League breaches case

- Manchester City guilty charges explained: Premier League's options, how appeal works, more

In Turkey, Mancini said that "Manchester City is not guilty and the fact of having a double contract isn't my problem but theirs, probably."

Mancini led City to its first titles after Abu Dhabi's ruling family had bought the club in 2008, winning the FA Cup in 2011 and in 2011-12 coaching the team to its first Premier League title in a half century.

He was fired days after a shocking loss to Wigan in the FA Cup final in 2013.

City has protested its innocence throughout the long-running case, which reached a milestone Tuesday when the Premier League published a verdict saying the club was "guilty of all charges related to serious breaches" of the competition's financial rules from 2009-18.
